verdicts.reason: A: headline, CTA and logo sit in a clear left column and are readable, with the product on its cream disc on the right. But the bottle hangs below the disc, the NEW FLAVOR badge is shrunk to a tiny unreadable dot pushed into the corner away from the product, and the bottom third is dead space. B: the white headline sits on the cream disc, so 'Blood Orange Sunset' is close to unreadable. The orange bottle is pulled off its disc and nearly disappears into the orange background, and the badge was turned into a pill shape (off-brand).

Both use the same broken layout. The white headline sits on the cream disc, so most of the title is unreadable. The bottle is pulled off its disc and fades into the orange background, and the empty disc collides with the logo and copy. A keeps the round badge but floats it in a stray ellipse far from the product. B squashes the badge into a pill next to the logo. The difference is too small to choose one.

A: the headline is readable on plain orange, but it breaks into three cramped lines. The bottle has lost its cream disc and is nearly invisible orange-on-orange in the middle. The CTA is pushed to the far right, cut off from the headline, with the empty disc and badge stacked above it, which jumbles the reading order. B: the white headline sits on the cream disc and is unreadable, the bottle is detached and washed out, and the pill badge is off-brand. A is less bad because its title can still be read.
